text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 detected — sudden spike in 5xx errors originating from region eu3 (edge gateway). Auto-alerting on-call and SRE. Dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/alerts/4898765432 · Logs: https://logs.redwood/streams/edge-eu3 · runbook: /runbooks/edge-5xx.md

maya: ack — I'm taking on-call. Starting triage. @sanjay can you grab gateway logs + backend traces?

sanjay: on it. quick scan shows a rapid rise in 502/504s starting ~14:01 UTC, concurrent increase in connection resets to mlworkers. sample from edge-proxy:
```
edge-proxy-1 | 2026-03-15T14:01:58Z | 502 | upstream_timeout | path=/v1/chat/stream
edge-proxy-2 | 2026-03-15T14:02:05Z | 504 | read_timeout | backend=mlworker-14
edge-proxy-3 | 2026-03-15T14:02:12Z | 502 | conn_reset | backend=mlworker-3
```
looks like backend latency or connection churn. CPU on mlworker pool eu3 is normal, but we see socket errors. grabbing tcpdump and backend logs now.

eric: I just checked infra side: no scheduled deploys in eu3, autoscaler didn't trigger. Netlook shows increased retransmits between edge-proxies and workers in eu3 AZ-b. Might be a network flap in that AZ. @netops-bot any BGP or link alerts?

netops-bot: Network alert: transient packet loss detected on eu3-azb between edge-subnet and worker-subnet from 14:00:50Z to 14:03:20Z. Severity: medium. CIRCUIT: eu3-azb-eth1.

maya: OK that matches. Customer impact estimate? CS/Support please assemble list of top customers in EU.

julie: pulling top traffic list. Early numbers: ~18% of requests in eu3 returned 5xx in the last 3m, spike most pronounced for chat/stream endpoints. Affected customers (by volume): AcmeCorp, PaperTrail, FinServX. Opening support RAs and drafting initial comms.

sanjay: mitigation plan options:
- immediate: steer ~50% of eu3 user traffic to eu-west-1 (gradual) to reduce pressure and avoid cross-region cold starts
- local: bounce edge-proxies in az-b and drain connections (risky during high traffic)
- long-term: circuit-break upstream to fail fast (introduce controlled fallbacks)

maya: prefer steering first to minimize churn. Sanjay, can you execute routing adjustment? Use redwoodctl so platform routing respects policy and no direct DNS flips.

sanjay: running: `redwoodctl traffic shift --from-region eu3 --to-region eu-west-1 --percent 50 --strategy gradual --window 5m`
```
> Scheduling traffic shift: from=eu3 to=eu-west-1 percent=50 strategy=gradual window=5m
> Operation id: shift-4898765432-01
```

eric: also adding short circuit-break at edge to reduce retry amplification: set `edge.timeout.upstream=1.5s` and `edge.retries=1` for chat routes. Applying now.

sanjay: routing op in flight. Observability: starting to see error-rate delta. Pre-mitigation 5xx rate: 18.3% for eu3. Post-10m into shift: 5xx rate down to 4.1% (aggregate), eu3 alone dropped to ~6.8%.

julie: telling CS to notify impacted customers with a brief note: "We detected a regional network disruption affecting some EU requests; we have shifted traffic and are monitoring. No data loss and normalizing for most customers." Draft pinned in #customer-comms for review.

maya: good. Next: follow-up actions — open ticket with cloud provider for eu3-azb network instability, schedule probe to reproduce, update runbook to include network-flap checklist. Also coordinate with on-call rotation so someone stays on watch for next 2 hours.

eric: we should also flag model-serving pools that had the most conn-resets (workers 3,14). I opened a task to run deeper heap/socket diagnostics on those hosts.

sanjay: confirmed: traffic shift completed, metrics show sustained reduction. Rolling back edge timeouts to normal once stabilization confirmed.

netops-bot: Update: cloud provider acknowledged packet-loss event in eu3-azb, mitigating at provider layer — ETA for full catheterization unknown.

maya: summary for status page: "Investigating: Elevated 5xx rates originating in EU region due to intermittent network errors between edge and worker subnets; mitigation applied by shifting traffic to eu-west-1. Error rates reduced substantially; monitoring continues." Julie, can you push this as a partial outage notification?

julie: Posted status page update (incident 4898765432). Also created a CS incident for top 5 impacted customers with suggested workaround: prefer multi-region endpoints.

sanjay: closing loop: recommend follow-ups — postmortem owner: @sanjay, due in 48h; runbook updates: add traffic-shift quick commands and provider contact template; infra hardening: add cross-AZ health checks for proxy-worker connectivity.

eric: adding one more FYI — we observed a small latency bump in eu-west-1 after shift (~60ms) but within SLA. No downstream degradations.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll stay watching for 30m then hand back to next on-call. If error-rate creeps above 5% we re-open and escalate to on-call-2. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update logged. Severity: SEV2 -> mitigation in place. Links: runbook, grafana, logs. Next update scheduled in 30m.

julie: note for postmortem: include timeline, customers impacted, exact routing commands used, and communications timeline.

sanjay: recording artifacts: `shift-4898765432-01` op log, tcpdump archive s3://incidents/4898765432/tcpdump-eu3-azb.pcap.gz, proxy logs snapshot.

maya: closing thread here — moving to watch channel. Thanks team. :heart:
